title: First-use flow is clear — hero text, wallet input, LOAD DEMO button, ANALYZE button
evidence: Landing page shows: hero 'Every wallet has a story' with subtitle explaining TEE-bound agent concept. WalletInput textarea with placeholder showing format examples. Two buttons: pink ANALYZE (disabled when empty) and transparent LOAD DEMO. Persona preview sidebar showing 'Same Trader · Two Selves' with Ethereum/Solana personas pre-displayed. Stats bar showing 4 CHAINS, 6,134 TRANSACTIONS, $4,527 NET PNL, TEE SEALED. Footer with OKX.AI Genesis attribution.
rationale: A first-time user can understand the product in 10 seconds from the hero text + persona preview. The LOAD DEMO button removes the friction of finding wallet addresses. Two clicks to start. Excellent first-use experience.
fix_guidance: No critical issues. Consider adding a 'How it works' tooltip near the ANALYZE button.

title: No phase navigation — auto-advancing flow gives user no control over pacing
evidence: Phases auto-advance via fixed timers: scanning(2s)→results(18s)→battle(38s)→compare(18s)→cta. No pause, skip, rewind, or navigation controls. If user wants to re-read a persona card or spends more time on results, the battle phase starts regardless. RoastBattle auto-advances rounds every 4 seconds — user can't control round pacing.
rationale: The auto-advancing flow is designed for a 76-second recorded demo, not interactive use. A real user would want to control the pace. The 38-second battle phase is particularly long — if the user isn't engaged, they may bounce.
fix_guidance: Add manual controls: 'Next' button for each phase, or click-to-advance. At minimum: pause button on roast battle. For demo recording: the current auto-advance is appropriate.

title: Input validation provides clear feedback — max 5 limit, empty check, error messages
evidence: WalletInput validates before submission: empty check ('Enter at least one wallet address'), max 5 ('Maximum 5 wallets for the demo'), address parsing with per-line error messages (shows which line failed). ANALYZE button disabled when textarea empty or loading. Error displayed in pink text below buttons. Placeholder shows format examples.
rationale: Good input validation UX. Errors appear on submit (not inline), which is acceptable for a 2-line textarea. The max-5 limit is reasonable for a demo. Could add inline address format validation as the user types.
fix_guidance: Consider adding real-time address format validation (turn input border green/red as user types valid/invalid addresses). Low priority for hackathon.

title: No loading/empty/error states for battle and compare phases — blank screen on failure
evidence: Scanning phase: TypingText 'Analyzing N wallets...' — good loading state. Results phase: persona cards render conditionally on data — if data is null, phase shows nothing. Battle phase: render guard `battleData &&` — if battleData is null, shows completely blank Terminal (plus 'Round X/Y' status text at bottom). Compare phase: same issue with compareData. Error state: none — catch blocks reset to landing silently.
rationale: The battle and compare phases have no fallback UI for when data is null. If a fetch fails (network issue, cache file missing), the user sees a blank screen for 38 seconds during battle phase with only 'Preparing battle...' text. This is the worst UX failure mode — silent blank screen with no indication of what went wrong or how to recover.
fix_guidance: Add error state: if battleData is null, show 'Could not load roast battle. Retry?' button. Add loading skeleton for battle/compare transitions. Show phase-appropriate empty states instead of blank screens.

title: Adequate action feedback — button state changes, typing animation, phase indicators
evidence: ANALYZE button: disabled during loading (opacity 30%), pink glow on hover. PaymentButton: 3-state transition (idle→simulating→done) with color changes. Scanning phase: typing animation with blinking cursor. RoastBattle: animated round transitions with colored borders (cyan/pink/yellow), speaker labels, round counter. PersonaCard: scale+opacity entrance animation. PatternCard: slide-in from left (AMPLIFY) or right (GUARD). All state changes have visual feedback.
rationale: Good observability for all intentional actions. User can always tell what's happening. The loading/scanning states are particularly well-done with the typing animation. The roast battle speaker transitions are visually clear.
fix_guidance: No action needed. Action feedback is well-implemented throughout the flow.
